title: Adjoint bilinear test for maps out of an inverse-image tensor
statement:
Let $h:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use compatible small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the specified sheaf inverse image $h^{-1}$, direct image $h_*$ and unit $\eta_h$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, let $M,N$ be sheaves of $R$-modules, and let $K$ be any sheaf of $h^{-1}R$-modules on $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Give $h_*K$ its $R$-action through $\eta_{h,R}:R\to h_*h^{-1}R$. Use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For an $h^{-1}R$-linear map $\alpha:h^{-1}(M\otimes_RN)\to K$, define the map of underlying sheaves
$$\widehat\alpha=h_*\alpha\circ\eta_{h,M\otimes_RN}:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow h_*K.$$
Then $\widehat\alpha$ is $R$-linear. The assignment $\alpha\mapsto\widehat\alpha$ is a bijection from the displayed module Hom set to $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M\otimes_RN,h_*K)$, natural in $M,N,K$; its underlying maps are exactly the adjuncts under the specified set-sheaf adjunction.

Let $\operatorname{Bilin}_R(M\times N,h_*K)$ denote maps of sheaves of sets that are $R(V)$-bilinear on sections over every site object $V$. The assignment
$$\alpha\longmapsto\bigl((s,t)\longmapsto\alpha_{T'\times_TV}(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))\bigr)$$
is a bijection onto $\operatorname{Bilin}_R(M\times N,h_*K)$, where $s\in M(V)$, $t\in N(V)$, pure tensors are their sheafification images, and $h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$ is the unit image. Consequently two such maps $\alpha,\beta$ are equal if and only if they agree on $h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$ for every $V,s,t$. No generation assumption on sections over objects of $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is imposed.

The following evaluations are included in the test. Suppose that for each scheme map $f$ under consideration and each commutative coefficient ring sheaf $S$ on its target, maps
$$b^f_{S,P,Q}:f^{-1}(P\otimes_SQ)\longrightarrow f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}S}f^{-1}Q$$
are supplied for $S$-module sheaves $P,Q$, and satisfy $b^f(f^{-1}(p\otimes q))=f^{-1}p\otimes f^{-1}q$ on all original unit sections. Neither invertibility nor naturality of the supplied maps is assumed.

For a ring map $\phi:R\to R'$ and $R'$-module sheaves $M,N$, let $\pi$ and $\pi'$ be the canonical maps from tensor over $R$ to tensor over $R'$, and from tensor over $h^{-1}R$ to tensor over $h^{-1}R'$, respectively; both send pure tensors to the corresponding pure tensors. The values of $b^h_{R',M,N}\circ h^{-1}\pi$ and $\pi'\circ b^h_{R,M,N}$ on $h^{-1}(s\otimes_Rt)$ are both $h^{-1}s\otimes_{h^{-1}R'}h^{-1}t$.

For a second scheme map $g:T''\to T'$, suppose a natural set-sheaf isomorphism $\delta:(h\circ g)^{-1}\cong g^{-1}h^{-1}$ is supplied, is compatible with the transported ring/module operations, and satisfies $\delta_H((h\circ g)^{-1}s)=g^{-1}h^{-1}s$ for every object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every $s\in H(V)$, the two sides being compared over $T''\times_TV\cong T''\times_{T'}(T'\times_TV)$ through the canonical fibre-product associator. Identify scalar rings along $\delta_R$. The values of
$$b^g\circ g^{-1}(b^h)\circ\delta_{M\otimes_RN}\quad\text{and}\quad(\delta_M\otimes\delta_N)\circ b^{h\circ g}$$
on $(h\circ g)^{-1}(s\otimes_Rt)$ are both $g^{-1}h^{-1}s\otimes g^{-1}h^{-1}t$, under the same associator identification of the objects. These assertions are evaluations of the displayed composites for supplied data, not existence assertions about $b$ or $\delta$.

proof.text: Put $L=h^{-1}$ and $V=h_*$ on set sheaves. The specified pro-etale construction is an adjunction with finite-limit-preserving $L$, on compatible small sites. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-construction] with $A=S=h^{-1}R$, $c=1_A$ and the canonical identification $|A|=L|R|$. Its functor $I$ identifies with the specified inverse image on modules: the underlying isomorphism $e_I:|I(X)|\cong L|X|$ preserves addition and scalar multiplication because both operations on the right are, by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the images under $L$ of the operations on $X$. Its functor $P$ identifies with the specified direct image of modules: $e_P:|P(K)|\cong V|K|$ preserves addition, and its scalar action is $V$ of the action on $K$, precomposed with the pair $(\eta_{h,R},e_P)$. Indeed the adjunct of the identity $L|R|\to L|R|$ is $\eta_{h,R}$. On sections this is precisely $r\cdot k=\eta_{h,R,V}(r)k$ over $T'\times_TV$. Thus these underlying isomorphisms are module isomorphisms to the actual functors in the statement, natural on module morphisms.

source.place: Tags 03D1 and 03D2, lemma-pushforward-module and lemma-pullback-module; operation comparisons for the specified inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport] to these functors. It supplies a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{h^{-1}R}(h^{-1}X,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,h_*K)$ whose underlying functions are the given set-sheaf adjuncts, after the module identifications in step 1. Since a set-sheaf adjunct is $h_*\alpha\circ\eta_{h,X}$, this proves that expression is $R$-linear, and proves surjectivity as well as injectivity on module morphisms. Specialize to $X=M\otimes_RN$. For clarity the forward linearity formula on sections is $\widehat\alpha_V(rx)=\alpha_{T'\times_TV}(\eta_R(r)\eta_X(x))=\eta_R(r)\widehat\alpha_V(x)$, with the identical addition formula. Linearity of the inverse adjunct, which cannot be inferred merely from original sections of the inverse image, is supplied by the cited transport bijection. Its naturality in $X,K$ gives naturality in $M,N,K$ by precomposing with the induced tensor morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, and Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, at the identity coefficient map

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $\mathcal F=M$, $\mathcal G=N$, $\mathcal H=h_*K$, using the $R$-action fixed in step 1. Its bijection sends a linear map $a:M\otimes_RN\to h_*K$ to $(s,t)\mapsto a_V(s\otimes t)$. Composing it with step 2 gives a bijection to exactly the set of bilinear sheaf maps specified in the item. Substituting the adjunct formula gives $a_V(s\otimes t)=\alpha_{T'\times_TV}(\eta_{h,M\otimes_RN,V}(s\otimes t))$, the displayed formula. This includes existence for every bilinear map and uniqueness of its inverse. Naturality in $K$ follows from both cited bijections. Naturality in $M,N$ follows directly from $(u\otimes v)(s\otimes t)=u(s)\otimes v(t)$: the two bilinear maps after precomposition have the same displayed value for every $V,s,t$.

source.place: Section 03EK, section-tensor-product, bilinear universal property following lemma-sheafification-tensor (Tag 0GMW)

proof.text: For two module maps $\alpha,\beta$, equality of their values on all original unit pure tensors is, by the formula in step 3, equality of their associated bilinear sheaf maps on every component and every pair of sections. The bijection in step 3 is injective, so $\alpha=\beta$. Conversely equal maps have equal values. This argument uses only the two established Hom-set bijections; it makes no assertion that original sections generate the sections on an arbitrary object of $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Agent deduction from the bijections of steps 2 and 3

proof.text: For coefficient change, write $x=s\otimes_Rt$ and use naturality of the specified unit with respect to $\pi$: $h^{-1}\pi(h^{-1}x)=h^{-1}(\pi(x))=h^{-1}(s\otimes_{R'}t)$. By the assumed normalization for the supplied $b^h_{R',M,N}$, its image is $h^{-1}s\otimes_{h^{-1}R'}h^{-1}t$. In the other composite, normalization of $b^h_{R,M,N}$ first gives $h^{-1}s\otimes_{h^{-1}R}h^{-1}t$, and the defining formula for $\pi'$ gives the same result. All maps can be read after restricting scalars to $h^{-1}R$; the underlying module inverse images agree because their additive structures are the same and their $h^{-1}R$-actions are obtained by applying $h^{-1}\phi$. This is compatibility of the defined actions with composition of sheaf maps, not an invertibility or naturality assertion about $b$.

source.place: Agent evaluation using the specified unit naturality and the supplied pure-tensor formulas; Section 03EK for tensor notation

proof.text: For composition, put $x=s\otimes_Rt$. The supplied normalization of $\delta$ sends $(h\circ g)^{-1}x$ to $g^{-1}(h^{-1}x)$. Naturality of the $g$-unit with respect to the sheaf map $b^h$ sends this under $g^{-1}(b^h)$ to $g^{-1}(b^h(h^{-1}x))=g^{-1}(h^{-1}s\otimes_{h^{-1}R}h^{-1}t)$. Here $h^{-1}s,h^{-1}t$ are sections over the site object $T'\times_TV$, so the assumed normalization of $b^g$ applies to them and yields $g^{-1}h^{-1}s\otimes g^{-1}h^{-1}t$. For the other composite, normalization of $b^{h\circ g}$ first gives $(h\circ g)^{-1}s\otimes(h\circ g)^{-1}t$. Applying $\delta_M\otimes\delta_N$ gives $\delta_M((h\circ g)^{-1}s)\otimes\delta_N((h\circ g)^{-1}t)$, which is the same result by the two supplied unit formulas. Every equality is over $T''\times_TV\cong T''\times_{T'}(T'\times_TV)$, and ring/module compatibility of $\delta$ makes the second tensor map linear after identifying scalar rings by $\delta_R$. The calculation uses no further property or existence of the supplied maps.
